newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up, rally in small-cap stocks.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up, rally in small-cap stocks.

text.p: Singapore shares bounced off their day's low to end in positive territory on Wednesday.
Dealers said the activity was mostly generated by retail investors and punters in small-capitalised stocks such as Labroy Marine and SM Summit, which hogged the actives lists.
U.S.-dollar denominated shares were firm on the back of the stronger greenback against the Singapore dollar.
Selected blue chips rose on thin volumes as most foreign funds rushed to Hong Kong, dealers said. The Hang Seng index rose 472.78 points to a record close of 13,766.65 on Wednesday.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended 5.63 points up at 2,221.15 after dropping to a low of 2,212.11. The index was led up mainly by Cycle & Carriage, which rose S$0.50 to S$16.90. Market turnover was an active 179 million and gainers outpaced losers by 232 to 120.
Hong Kong Land Holdings stock barely moved despite an "outrageous" price paid for a site in Hong Kong as the company had a limited land bank for development, dealers said.
Armstrong hogged the actives with more than 15 million shares traded after a research house recommended an accumulate on the stock. Cerebos fell S$0.30 to S$10.50.
